questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests hands-on ability to apply Kubernetes NetworkPolicy for multi-namespace isolation and least privilege, including default-deny and per-port allow rules, plus practical troubleshooting steps.

## Key Concepts
- NetworkPolicy basics
- namespaceSelector and podSelector
- Ingress vs Egress rules and reciprocity
- Troubleshooting pod reachability with test pods

## Code Example
```yaml
# api-prod-default-deny
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-prod-default-deny
  namespace: api-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-prod
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
```

```yaml
# api-prod-to-logging (allow egress to logging)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-prod-to-logging
  namespace: api-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-prod
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: logging
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

```yaml
# logging-accept-api-prod (allow ingress from api-prod to logging)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: logging-accept-api-prod
  namespace: logging
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: logging
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: api-prod
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

```yaml
# api-prod-to-db (allow egress to db-prod on 5432)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-prod-to-db
  namespace: api-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-prod
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: db-prod
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5432
```

```yaml
# db-accept-api-prod (allow ingress from api-prod to db)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: db-accept-api-prod
  namespace: db-prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: api-prod
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5432
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you verify no other cross-namespace traffic is allowed after policies apply?
- How would you roll back if a required path is blocked by policy?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to diagnose dynamic mutation timing, rollout semantics, and safe rollback in a mutating webhook scenario.

## Key Concepts
- MutatingAdmissionWebhook
- Rollout strategies and canaries
- kubectl rollout and validation

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
NAMESPACE=fin
missing=()
for d in $(kubectl get deploy -n "$NAMESPACE" -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  containers=$(kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" get deploy "$d" -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[*].name}')
  if [[ ! $containers == *sidecar* ]]; then
    missing+=("$d")
  fi
done
if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "Missing sidecar in: ${missing[*]}"
  exit 1
else
  echo "All deployments include sidecar"
fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you implement a canary rollout to validate webhook mutation before full rollout?
- How would you revert to a previous webhook version and confirm no pods are missing the sidecar after rollback?

Why This Is Asked
Tests practical RBAC debugging: confirming service accounts can read Secrets and how to lift permissions safely. It mirrors real-world issues where apps fail due to missing or mis-scoped access rather than code bugs.

Key Concepts
- RBAC: Roles and RoleBindings
- Secrets: access via API and mount points
- ServiceAccount scope to a namespace
- kubectl can-i, kubectl rollout restart

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  namespace: myns
  name: secret-reader
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: secret-reader-binding
  namespace: myns
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: my-app-sa
  namespace: myns
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: secret-reader
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

Follow-up Questions
- If 401/403 persist after the fix, what next diagnostics would you run (e.g., PodSecurityPolicy, namespace scoping, API server audit logs)?
- How would you automate this RBAC check as part of a CI cycle to prevent regressions?
